notes: OCR B line garbled (netuficaliyan = netuñcaliyan, i.e. netuñcaḻiyaṉ). kuv-anke: book (sec. 7.16.2) analyses as kuvanku + e "to Kuvan"; recorded as stem kuvan + dative -ke. text_B: kani-i nata-siri-y kuva[n*]... vel-arai-y nikamatu kaviti-iy kalitika antai asutan pina-u kotupiton
notes: Gap of ~30 cm after kuva[n*] (flaked stone). nikamatu "merchant guild" (role OTHER, an institution; genitive from translation "of the merchant guild"). kaviti = ancient title (note 9). kalitika: note 10 "Read kalatika", kal "pearl" + atikan "superintendent". antai = honorific suffix for an elder (note 11) -> TITLE_OR_OCCUPATION. pina-u: meaning uncertain ("partition or cleft", translated "cave(?)"); B OCR "ріпа-и" read pina-u (A line shows long nā). Hyphen in vel-arai is a compound/pause, not a suffix.
kotiyavan = kottiyavan < kottu (note 3); "the inscription" understood (note 4).
Composite name cantan + aritan (note 2). "the cave" understood (note 4).
nikamator = nikamattor, nikamattu + or "members of the merchant guild" (note 3, sec. 7.16.2); role TITLE_OR_OCCUPATION (judgement). "the stone beds" understood (note 5).

text_B: nelveli-iy cilivan atinan veliyan mulakai kotupiton

pankata construed as pankatu + a "of Pankat(u)" (note 3). Hyphen in ar-itan marks the pause between r and a (sec. 6.19.2), not a suffix. "the drip ledge" understood.
upacan = upaccan "preceptor" < upadhyaya (note 1). Hyphen in par-acu is a pause (note 2).

Inscription engraved right-to-left and upside down.
kura "cutting" (cf. LT kurai, note 5) of the drip ledge. [n*] restored (note 8). Incomplete at end.

B OCR "pitam" corrected to pitan from A line ("pi tà na") and note 5 (pittan). itta: cf. LT itai/ittai "this" accusative (note 6). vepon = veppon "has endowed" (note 7). Translation OCR "has endowed {15.8" read as "this (section)" per note 8.

Translation line not captured by the OCR (Tamil-script line only). Name of donor; earliest occurrence of the velar nasal n (note 2).
kuvira = kuviran + a "of Kuviran"; the PNG suffix -an is elided before genitive -a (note 2, sec. 7.16.6). Second akshara damaged.
amanan "Jaina monk" < samana (note 1). matirai = Madurai (note 2). utayana(n) + sa: unique Prakrit genitive -sa, PNG -(a)n dropped (note 3). Restored danda [|*] after urai dropped.
cf. hariti (Pkt.). Last letter on the adjacent bed.
matira variant of matirai (note 3). visuvan = vissuvan (note 4).
centa(n) + a; PNG suffix -an elided before genitive -a (note 2). OCR "cénta" (ē).
B OCR "patin-[ajr" corrected from A line ("pa ti ṉa [ū] ra"). atai = antai, masc. honorific with nasal omitted (note 4).

vel: title of an ancient clan of chieftains, here part of a personal name (note 2), so role PERSONAL_NAME.
titti-il is a place name; final -a is the genitive suffix (note 2). Collective gift by the village (note 3).
elai- probably a variant of itai (note 4). ariti-n construed as ariti + (i)n "of Ariti" (note 5). -y- is a glide, recorded as a suffix following the task's example.

vempirrur = vempil + tt + ur (note 3). perayam "large tank" (note 4); hyphens in per-ay-am appear to be pause marks, not suffixes (OCR "рег-ау-ат"). cetavar cf. LT ceytavar, plural verb implying the village assembly (note 6).
Symbol at end (note 3). matiray variant of matirai (note 4). Composite name "Atan, son of Atan" (note 6).

Fragment, incomplete at either end; no translation printed. Note 1: "Read nakan" (scribal use of dental n for alveolar n initially). Role of nakan as a personal name is a guess from the commentary parallels (nakan occurs as a name in Nos. 48, 72).

Book (sec. 7.16.2) analyses as matiraiku + e; case-ending -ke employed in a possessive-locative sense (note 2). Recorded as genitive following the translation "Of". Printed with a colon indicating that donors in Nos. 39-45 are all from Matirai.
B OCR "ири-уашКап" restored from A line ("ū pu vā ṇi ka ṉa"): uppu "salt" + vanikan "merchant" (note 2). The five donors of Nos. 39-43 made a collective gift (note 4).
